title: Principal Series Representations of Gl N over a Finite Field

items.title: Diagonal torus characters and the Weyl action
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $q$ be a prime power, and put $G=\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$
with diagonal torus $T$, upper triangular Borel $B=T\ltimes U$, monomial subgroup
$N$ and Weyl group $W=N/T\cong S_n$
(def-standard-subgroups-of-gl-n-over-a-finite-field,
def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n). For $w\in S_n$ let
$\dot w:=P_w\in G$ be the permutation matrix of $w$, so that
$\dot w^{-1}\,t\,\dot w$ is diagonal for every $t\in T$. A **character** of $T$ is
a group homomorphism $\chi:T\to\mathbb C^\times$; write
$\widehat T:=\operatorname{Hom}(T,\mathbb C^\times)$ for the group of characters,
with pointwise multiplication and the trivial character $1_{\widehat T}$.

**Coordinates.** Since $T\cong(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n$ via
$t=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,\dots,t_n)\mapsto(t_1,\dots,t_n)$, the assignment
$\chi\mapsto(\chi_1,\dots,\chi_n)$ with
$\chi(\operatorname{diag}(t_1,\dots,t_n))=\prod_{i=1}^n\chi_i(t_i)$ is a bijection
from $\widehat T$ onto the set of $n$-tuples of characters of
$\mathbb F_q^\times$; the $\chi_i$, given by
$\chi_i(a)=\chi(\operatorname{diag}(1,\dots,a,\dots,1))$ with $a$ in the $i$-th
position, are the **coordinates** of $\chi$, and the tuple of coordinates
determines $\chi$ by the displayed product formula.

**The Weyl action and equal-character blocks.** The group $S_n$ acts on
$\widehat T$ by
$$(w\cdot\chi)(t):=\chi(\dot w^{-1}t\dot w)\qquad(w\in S_n,\ \chi\in\widehat T,\ t\in T),$$
and for the coordinates this reads
$$(w\cdot\chi)_j=\chi_{w^{-1}(j)}\qquad(1\le j\le n):$$
the action permutes the coordinates. For $\chi\in\widehat T$ define the **Weyl
stabiliser** $W_\chi:=\{\,w\in S_n:w\cdot\chi=\chi\,\}$. A permutation $w$ lies in
$W_\chi$ exactly when $\chi_{w^{-1}(j)}=\chi_j$ for all $j$, that is, exactly when
$w$ preserves every level set $\{\,j:\chi_j=a\,\}$, $a\in\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb F_q^\times,\mathbb C^\times)$. These
level sets, the orbits of $W_\chi$ on $\{1,\dots,n\}$, are the **equal-character
blocks** of $\chi$; they are the maximal subsets on which $\chi$ is constant. If
they have sizes $n_1,\dots,n_k$, with $n_1+\cdots+n_k=n$, then $W_\chi$ is the
Young subgroup $S_{n_1}\times\cdots\times S_{n_k}\le S_n$ of permutations
preserving each block, so that $|W_\chi|=\prod_{r=1}^kn_r!$.

**Intrinsic Coxeter system.** The intrinsic Coxeter generators of $W_\chi$ are the
transpositions of successive elements of each equal-character block, listed in
increasing order. They need not be adjacent transpositions of $S_n$: for
$\chi=(a,b,a)$ with $a\ne b$ the block $\{1,3\}$ produces the generator $(1\,3)$.
To record this system choose a permutation $\sigma\in S_n$ for which
$\eta:=\sigma\cdot\chi$ has each equal-character block contiguous, the blocks
being ordered by the first occurrence of their character in $\chi$ and the order
inside each block preserved; such a $\sigma$ is obtained by listing the blocks in
that order. Write $S_\eta$ for the set of ambient adjacent transpositions $s_i$
with $i,i+1$ inside one block of $\eta$, and put
$S_\chi:=\sigma^{-1}S_\eta\sigma$. Then $(W_\chi,S_\chi)$ is the Coxeter system
obtained by transporting the product system of the standard contiguous Young
subgroup $W_\eta$. The **intrinsic length** on $W_\chi$ is transported along this
identification from the length of the product system; it is not the ambient
inversion length $\ell$ of $S_n$, and $S_\chi$ need not consist of simple
reflections of $W$.

**Regular characters.** Call $\chi$ **regular** when its coordinates are pairwise
distinct, that is, when every equal-character block has size $1$; then
$W_\chi=1$, $k=n$ and $S_\chi=\varnothing$. At the other extreme, since
$\mathbb F_2^\times$ is the trivial group, for $q=2$ there is exactly one character
of $T$, and then $W_\chi=S_n$ and $k=1$.
items.strategy: Factor the character through the coordinate projections of $T$. Direct matrix calculation gives $(\dot w^{-1}t\dot w)_{ii}=t_{w(i)}$, hence $(w\cdot\chi)_j=\chi_{w^{-1}(j)}$. The stabilizer consists exactly of permutations preserving each equal-character set. Ordering these finite sets and their first occurrences defines the sorting permutation explicitly. Conjugation by it identifies the stabilizer with the standard contiguous Young subgroup, and transports that product Coxeter system back. There is no arbitrary choice. In particular, ambient adjacent equal coordinates cannot be used to generate an unsorted stabilizer.

items.title: Idempotents lift through adically complete quotients
items.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative $\mathbb C$-algebra, let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal, and
suppose that $R$ is $I$-adically complete and separated, so that
$R\cong\varprojlim_{n\ge1}R/I^n$
(def-separated-and-complete-filtered-module, def-adic-completion-of-a-module);
over a complete local ring $R$ one may take $I$ its maximal ideal. Let $A$ be an
associative unital $R$-algebra which is finitely generated as an $R$-module and
complete for the $I$-adic topology of the filtration $I^nA$, $n\ge0$, so that
$A\to\varprojlim_{n\ge1}A/I^nA$ is an isomorphism
(def-adic-topology-on-a-module). If $x\in A$ satisfies
$x^2-x\in IA$, then there exists $e\in A$ with
$$e^2=e,\qquad e\equiv x\pmod{IA}.$$
Consequently: (1) every idempotent of $A/IA$ is the image of an idempotent of
$A$; (2) for every finite family of pairwise orthogonal idempotents
$\bar x_1,\dots,\bar x_k$ of $A/IA$ there are pairwise orthogonal idempotents
$e_1,\dots,e_k\in A$ with $e_i\equiv\bar x_i\pmod{IA}$ for all $i$, and if
$\bar x_1+\cdots+\bar x_k=1$ they may be chosen with
$e_1+\cdots+e_k=1$. Neither assertion uses a choice principle.
items.strategy: Put $y=2x-1$ and $\varepsilon=y^2-1\in IA$. The binomial series $f(\varepsilon)=\sum_{m\ge0}\binom{-1/2}{m}\varepsilon^m$ converges because $\varepsilon^m\in I^mA$ and the filtration is complete and separated. Multiplication is continuous; the formal scalar identity $(1+z)f(z)^2=1$ therefore gives $(yf(\varepsilon))^2=1$, since $y$ commutes with $\varepsilon$ and its series. Hence $e=(1+yf(\varepsilon))/2$ is an idempotent congruent to $x$. For finitely many orthogonal quotient idempotents, lift the first and work next in $(1-e)A(1-e)$. This corner is a complete separated direct summand (the continuous idempotent projection is $a\mapsto(1-e)a(1-e)$). Compressed representatives are only approximate idempotents; apply the same series there to obtain genuine idempotents. Iterate finitely. If the quotient family sums to $1$, take the final lift to be the complement of the preceding lifts. No countable choice or Complete Nakayama is used.

items.title: The trace form detects semisimplicity over the complex numbers
items.statement: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional associative $\mathbb C$-algebra with unit, and let $(\cdot,\cdot):A\times A\to\mathbb C$ be the **trace form** $(a,b):=\operatorname{tr}(L_{ab})$, where $L_c:A\to A$ is left multiplication by $c$. Then $(\cdot,\cdot)$ is a symmetric associative bilinear form, and it is nondegenerate if and only if $A$ is semisimple. Moreover every semisimple finite-dimensional $\mathbb C$-algebra $A$ is isomorphic to a finite product $\prod_{i=1}^r\operatorname M_{d_i}(\mathbb C)$, its simple modules are the $d_i$-dimensional natural modules, and the trace form is the product of the nondegenerate matrix trace pairings.
items.strategy: The form is symmetric and satisfies $(ab,c)=(a,bc)$ because $L_{(ab)c}=L_{abc}=L_{a(bc)}$. If $A$ is semisimple, Wedderburn--Artin gives matrix factors over finite-dimensional complex division algebras; each such division algebra is $\mathbb C$, since every element has an eigenvalue as a left-multiplication operator and its difference from that scalar cannot be invertible. Thus $A\cong\prod_i\operatorname M_{d_i}(\mathbb C)$ ([[thm-wedderburn-artin-theorem]], [[thm-uniqueness-of-wedderburn-artin-data]]); on each matrix factor the trace form is the matrix trace pairing $(X,Y)\mapsto d_i\operatorname{tr}(XY)$, which is nondegenerate, so the product form is nondegenerate. Conversely, the Jacobson radical $J(A)$ is nilpotent and $A/J(A)$ is semisimple by [[thm-jacobson-radical-is-nilpotent-and-the-quotient-is-semisimple]]; for $x\in J(A)$ and $b\in A$ the element $xb$ lies in $J(A)$ and is therefore nilpotent, so $(x,b)=0$ for every $b$. If the trace form is nondegenerate this forces $x=0$, hence $J(A)=0$ and $A$ is semisimple. The description of the simple modules is the standard Wedderburn--Artin description. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Constituent multiplicities are dimensions of simple modules over the endomorphism algebra
items.statement: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional semisimple $\mathbb C$-algebra, let $M$ be a finite-dimensional semisimple $A$-module and put $E:=\operatorname{End}_A(M)$. Let $V_1,\dots,V_r$ be pairwise non-isomorphic simple $A$-modules with $M\cong\bigoplus_{i=1}^r V_i^{\oplus m_i}$, $m_i\ge1$. Then: (1) $E$ is a semisimple $\mathbb C$-algebra and there is an isomorphism $E\cong\prod_{i=1}^r\operatorname M_{m_i}(\mathbb C)$; (2) for every $i$ the space $S_i:=\operatorname{Hom}_A(V_i,M)$ is a simple $E$-module of dimension $m_i$, and $i\mapsto S_i$ is a bijection from $\{1,\dots,r\}$ onto the set of isomorphism classes of simple $E$-modules; (3) the multiplicity $m_i$ of $V_i$ in $M$ equals $\dim_{\mathbb C}S_i$. In particular, if $E$ is semisimple and $E\cong\operatorname{End}_A(M)$, then the constituents of $M$ are indexed by the isomorphism classes of simple $E$-modules and the multiplicity of the constituent attached to a simple $E$-module $S$ is $\dim_{\mathbb C}S$.
items.strategy: By complete reducibility fix an isotypic decomposition $M=\bigoplus_iM_i$ with $M_i\cong V_i^{\oplus m_i}$; Schur's lemma gives $\operatorname{Hom}_A(V_i,V_j)=0$ for $i\ne j$ and $\operatorname{End}_A(V_i)=\mathbb C$, so restriction of endomorphisms to the isotypic components yields $E\cong\prod_i\operatorname{End}_A(M_i)\cong\prod_i\operatorname M_{m_i}(\mathbb C)$, which is (1) and identifies the simple $E$-modules with the natural $\mathbb C^{m_i}$ ([[thm-endomorphism-ring-of-a-finite-direct-sum-as-hom-matrices]], [[thm-schurs-lemma-for-modules]]). For (2), $S_i=\operatorname{Hom}_A(V_i,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(V_i,M_i)$ is a left $E$-module by postcomposition and has dimension $m_i$ by Schur; evaluation identifies it with the natural simple $E$-module of the $i$-th matrix factor. Part (3) is immediate. If $E$ is only known to be abstractly isomorphic to $\operatorname{End}_A(M)$ the indexing transports along the isomorphism, and dimension is preserved by any algebra isomorphism. No choice principle is used beyond finite-dimensional linear algebra.

items.title: The generic type-A Hecke algebra
items.statement: Let $A:=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ be the ring of Laurent polynomials in one indeterminate. For $n\ge2$ the **generic type-A Hecke algebra** $H_v(n)$ is the associative unital $A$-algebra presented by generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ and the relations $$T_i^2=(v-1)T_i+v,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1}\ (1\le i\le n-2),\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\ (|i-j|>1),$$ the **RG-13 quadratic normalization** $(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$. For $n\le1$ set $H_v(n):=A$. For $w\in S_n$ and any reduced word $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_\ell}$ put $T_w:=T_{i_1}\cdots T_{i_\ell}$; by the type-A Matsumoto lemma ([[lem-type-a-reduced-words-are-connected-by-braid-moves]]) any two reduced words for $w$ are related by the braid and commutation relations of the presentation, so $T_w$ is well defined, and $T_1=1$. For a commutative $A$-algebra $R$ with structure map $\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]\to R$, $v\mapsto v_0\in R^\times$, write $R\otimes_AH_v(n)$ (or $H_{v_0}(n)$) for the **specialization**. Two specializations are used on this page: $v\mapsto1$ (the group algebra of $S_n$) and $v\mapsto q$, where $q$ is the prime power defining $\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$ (the finite Hecke algebra). **Dictionary to the published Soergel normalization.** The item [[def-type-a-hecke-algebra-in-soergel-normalization]] presents the same algebra over $\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ with the parameter $q=v^{-2}$, i.e. with quadratic relation $T_i^2=(q-1)T_i+q$ for that $q$; substituting $q=v_{\text{here}}$ translates between the two conventions. This page owns the specialization to the finite field and the Tits deformation; the Soergel page owns its self-contained presentation and standard basis, which is not duplicated here.
items.strategy: Definition plus the standard dictionary between the two normalizations; well-definedness of $T_w$ is exactly the type-A Matsumoto lemma. The presentation is the free unital associative $A$-algebra on $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ modulo the displayed two-sided ideal, so no existence or finiteness statement is assumed. The comparison with the Soergel normalization is a change of variables $q=v^{-2}$ in the quadratic relation only; both are records of the same deformation over the respective Laurent rings.

items.title: The principal series module of GL_n over a finite field
items.statement: Let $n\ge1$, let $q$ be a prime power, put $G=\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$ with Borel $B=T\ltimes U$, and let $\chi\in\widehat T$ be a character of the diagonal torus ([[def-diagonal-torus-characters-and-weyl-action]]). Since $B=T\ltimes U$ and $T\cong B/U$, extend $\chi$ to a character $\widetilde\chi$ of $B$ by $\widetilde\chi(lu):=\chi(l)$ ($l\in T$, $u\in U$); this is the **inflation** of $\chi$ from $T$ to $B$ and is trivial on $U$ ([[def-harish-chandra-induction-and-restriction-for-finite-gl-n]]). The **principal series module** attached to $\chi$ is the complex $G$-module $$I(\chi):=R_T^G(\chi)=\operatorname{Ind}_B^G\bigl(\operatorname{Inf}_T^B\chi\bigr)= \{\,f:G\to\mathbb C \;:\; f(gb)=\widetilde\chi(b)^{-1}f(g)\ \ \forall\, g\in G,\,b\in B\,\},$$ with $(g_0\cdot f)(g):=f(g_0^{-1}g)$ ([[def-induced-r-linear-g-module-by-h-covariant-functions]]); here $R_T^G$ is Harish--Chandra induction from the split Levi $T$ ([[def-harish-chandra-induction-and-restriction-for-finite-gl-n]]). Equivalently $I(\chi)=\operatorname{Ind}_B^G(\widetilde\chi)$. Its dimension is $\dim_{\mathbb C}I(\chi)=[G:B]=\prod_{i=1}^n\frac{q^i-1}{q-1}$, and for $\chi'\in\widehat T$ one has $I(\chi)\cong I(\chi')$ whenever $\chi'=w\cdot\chi$ for some $w\in S_n$ (proved below in the endomorphism item). For the trivial character $1$ one has $I(1)=R_T^G(1)$.
items.strategy: Definition of the induced module together with the standard function model and the dimension count. The inflation is the pullback along the projection $B\to B/U\cong T$, so it is a character of $B$ with kernel containing $U$; the function model is the usual realisation of $\operatorname{Ind}_B^G$ by $B$-covariant functions, and its dimension is the index $[G:B]\dim\chi$ by [[cor-dimension-of-an-induced-finite-dimensional-representation]]. The stabiliser statement $I(\chi)\cong I(w\cdot\chi)$ is proved by equality of the Mackey character pairings and complete reducibility; it is recorded here only as orientation and is proved in the endomorphism item. No choice principle is used.

items.title: The standard basis of the generic type-A Hecke algebra
items.statement:
In the generic type-A Hecke algebra $H_v(n)$ over $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ with
generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$, the quadratic relations
$(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$, the braid relations and the distant commutations, and with
$T_w$ the product of the $T_i$ along a reduced word for $w\in S_n$
(def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra):

1. $\{T_w:w\in S_n\}$ is an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$; in particular $H_v(n)$ is
free of rank $n!$ over $A$;
2. for every $w\in S_n$ and every $1\le i\le n-1$,
$$T_wT_i=T_{ws_i}\quad\text{if }\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)+1,\qquad T_wT_i=(v-1)T_w+v\,T_{ws_i}\quad\text{if }\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)-1,$$
where $\ell$ is the inversion length of $S_n$
(def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n); consequently the rule rewrites
every monomial in the generators as an $A$-linear combination of the $T_w$.

No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Derive the change in inversion count under each adjacent swap and use bubble sorting to show that inversion count is minimal word length. Prove reduced-word connectivity by induction on length: identical last letters reduce immediately; distinct final descents are either disjoint, giving a commutation, or adjacent on a descending triple, giving the braid move. On the free A-module with basis e_w, define rho_i by the ascent/descent rule. Check the quadratic relation directly, distant commutation in four disjoint-pair cases, and the adjacent braid relation in the six possible one-line orders of three adjacent values. This gives a right H_v(n)-module; applying a relation to e_id proves independence, while the multiplication rule proves spanning.

Jay Taylor, Finite Reductive Groups - Definition 5.13 and Remark 5.14 (generic Hecke algebra), printed pp. 44-45

items.title: Formal triviality of a semisimple one-parameter deformation
items.statement:
Let $R=\mathbb C[\![t]\!]$ be the ring of formal power series in one variable and
let $A$ be an associative unital $R$-algebra which is free of finite rank as an
$R$-module. If $A/tA\cong\prod_{i=1}^r\operatorname M_{d_i}(\mathbb C)$ as
$\mathbb C$-algebras, then
$$A\cong\prod_{i=1}^r\operatorname M_{d_i}(R)$$
as $R$-algebras. Moreover every $R$-linear endomorphism of a finite free
$R$-module whose reduction modulo $t$ is an isomorphism is itself an
isomorphism: the determinant of such a map has nonzero constant term, hence is
a unit of the local ring $R$. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Lift one diagonal primitive idempotent $e_i$ from each matrix block by [[lem-lifting-idempotents-in-complete-deformation-algebras]], and put $V_i=Ae_i$. Right multiplication by $e_i$ is an idempotent $R$-linear projection on the free module $A$, with image $V_i$ and kernel $A(1-e_i)$. Lift a finite basis of each of these two summands modulo $t$ into that summand. Their union has a square coordinate matrix invertible modulo $t$, so its determinant has nonzero constant term and is a unit, by [[prop-units-in-an-adically-complete-ring]] after dividing by that constant term. Its adjugate is an inverse, so the union is a basis of $A$. The projection is diagonal on this basis, proving $V_i$ is free of rank $d_i$ and reduces to the natural module of the $i$th matrix block. The left action gives $A\to\prod_i\operatorname{End}_R(V_i)$; modulo $t$ this is the faithful sum of natural representations, an isomorphism $\prod_iM_{d_i}(\mathbb C)\to\prod_iM_{d_i}(\mathbb C)$. Source and target are free of the same rank $\sum_i d_i^2$. Again the determinant unit criterion makes the action map an isomorphism. This explicitly supplies the direct-summand freeness and residue-isomorphism steps suppressed in Losev Theorem 2.6, Step 5. No Complete Nakayama, projective-module theorem or dependent choice is invoked.

references.title: Ivan Losev, Lecture 8: Representations of GL_n(F_q) - Section 2.3, Theorem 2.6, Step 5 (free direct summands and the residue-isomorphism criterion, expanded by a determinant proof), PDF p. 5
Olivier Dudas and Jean Michel, Lectures on Finite Reductive Groups and Their Representations - Section 11.2 (flatness of Hecke algebras and Tits' deformation theorem), printed p. 47

items.title: The spherical principal series is the flag permutation module
items.statement: Let $1\in\widehat T$ be the trivial character and let $G=\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$ with Borel $B$. Then $I(1)=R_T^G(1)=\operatorname{Ind}_B^G(1)$ is isomorphic, as a complex $G$-module, to the permutation module $\mathbb C[G/B]$ on the left cosets of $B$, and hence to the permutation module on the complete flags of $\mathbb F_q^n$: under the $G$-equivariant bijection $G/B\to\{\text{complete flags}\}$, $gB\mapsto gV_\bullet$, the induced module corresponds to the module of complex functions on complete flags with $G$ acting by translation. Its dimension is $[G:B]=\#\{\text{complete flags}\}=\prod_{i=1}^n\frac{q^i-1}{q-1}$.
items.strategy: The trivial character of $T$ inflates to the trivial character of $B$, so $I(1)=\operatorname{Ind}_B^G(1)$; the identification of the induction of the trivial representation with the permutation representation on the left cosets is [[thm-induction-of-the-trivial-representation-is-the-permutation-representation-on-left-cosets]], and the identification of $G/B$ with complete flags is [[thm-complete-flags-form-gl-n-over-b]] transported along the equivariant bijection. The dimension is the index $[G:B]$ computed in [[def-principal-series-module-for-finite-gl-n]]. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Mackey support for homomorphisms between principal series
items.statement: Let $\chi,\chi'\in\widehat T$. Then the Harish--Chandra adjunction $\operatorname{Hom}_G(R_T^G(\chi),R_T^G(\chi'))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(\chi,{}^*R_T^G(R_T^G(\chi')))$ combined with the parabolic Mackey formula for the pair of Borel subgroups yields an isomorphism of $\mathbb C$-vector spaces $$\operatorname{Hom}_G\bigl(I(\chi),I(\chi')\bigr)\;\cong\;\bigoplus_{w\in S_n}\operatorname{Hom}_T\bigl(\chi,{}^w\chi'\bigr),$$ where ${}^w\chi'$ is the conjugate character $t\mapsto\chi'(\dot w^{-1}t\dot w)= (w\cdot\chi')(t)$ ([[def-conjugate-representation-and-conjugate-character]]). Each summand is $\mathbb C$ if $\chi=w\cdot\chi'$ and $0$ otherwise, so $$\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_G\bigl(I(\chi),I(\chi')\bigr)=\#\{\,w\in S_n:\chi=w\cdot\chi'\,\}$$ and in particular $\operatorname{Hom}_G(I(\chi),I(\chi'))\ne0$ precisely when $\chi'$ lies in the $S_n$-orbit of $\chi$. Moreover the Mackey decomposition exhibits a canonical basis of $\operatorname{Hom}_G(I(\chi),I(\chi'))$ indexed by the set $\{\,w:\chi=w\cdot\chi'\,\}$.
items.strategy: Apply Harish--Chandra adjunction ([[thm-harish-chandra-adjunction-for-finite-gl-n]]) with $L=T$ and the Harish--Chandra restriction ${}^*R_T^G$; the Mackey formula ([[thm-parabolic-mackey-formula-for-finite-gl-n]], claim 2, special case $\alpha=\beta=(1^n)$) gives $${}^*R_T^G\bigl(R_T^G(\chi')\bigr)\cong\bigoplus_{w\in S_n}{}^w\chi',$$ because for $\alpha=\beta=(1^n)$ one has $C_w=L\cap M_w=T$, $A_w=D_w=\{1\}$ and $R_{C_w}^L=R_T^T=\operatorname{id}$, and the representatives of the double cosets $B\backslash G/B$ are the permutation matrices $\dot w$, one per $w\in S_n$. For one-dimensional characters over $\mathbb C$ one has $\dim\operatorname{Hom}_T(\chi,{}^w\chi')\in\{0,1\}$ with value $1$ exactly when $\chi=w\cdot\chi'$: this is the $T$-intertwiner dimension computed by [[thm-character-inner-product-computes-intertwiner-dimension]] (or Schur's lemma for one-dimensional modules). The basis statement is the transport of the displayed direct sum decomposition. No choice principle is used; all sums are finite.

Olivier Dudas and Jean Michel, Lectures on Finite Reductive Groups and Their Representations - Section 11.3 (Mackey formula for a split torus), printed pp. 47-49

items.title: The Weyl stabiliser controls the endomorphisms of a principal series
items.statement: Let $\chi,\chi'\in\widehat T$ and let $W_\chi\le S_n$ be the Weyl stabiliser of $\chi$ ([[def-diagonal-torus-characters-and-weyl-action]]). Then: (1) $\operatorname{Hom}_G(I(\chi),I(\chi'))\ne0$ if and only if $\chi'=w\cdot\chi$ for some $w\in S_n$, and in that case $\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_G(I(\chi),I(\chi'))=\#\{\,u\in S_n:\chi=u\cdot\chi'\,\}\le|W_\chi|$; (2) in particular $$\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{End}_G\bigl(I(\chi)\bigr)=|W_\chi|=\prod_{r=1}^kn_r!,$$ where $n_1,\dots,n_k$ are the sizes of the equal-character blocks of $\chi$; (3) $I(\chi)\cong I(w\cdot\chi)$ for every $w\in S_n$, though conjugation of functions is not an intertwiner for the fixed Borel. All statements hold over $\mathbb C$ for every prime power $q$ and every character $\chi$; no splitting hypothesis beyond $\mathbb C$ being a splitting field for the finite groups $T$ and $S_n$ is needed.
items.strategy: The Mackey support lemma [[lem-mackey-support-for-homs-between-finite-principal-series]] gives the Hom dimension as the number of Weyl elements carrying the target character to the source. If the characters lie in one Weyl orbit this number is exactly $N=|W_\chi|=|W_{\chi'}|$, giving (1) and (2). To prove (3), use [[thm-character-inner-product-computes-intertwiner-dimension]]: the characters $c,c'$ of the two modules have $\langle c,c\rangle=\langle c',c'\rangle=\langle c,c'\rangle=\langle c',c\rangle=N$, so $\langle c-c',c-c'\rangle=0$. Positivity of the finite class-function inner product gives $c=c'$. By Maschke and Schur, the multiplicity of every simple $V$ is $\langle c,\chi_V\rangle$, since each finite-dimensional complex division endomorphism ring is $\mathbb C$ (an endomorphism has an eigenvalue and a nonzero noninvertible difference from a scalar must vanish). Thus the two semisimple modules have the same finite simple decomposition and are isomorphic. This argument uses no conjugation of the fixed Borel and no arbitrary choice.

Olivier Dudas and Jean Michel, Lectures on Finite Reductive Groups and Their Representations - Section 11.3, equation (11.7) (dimension |W(L,N)^F| of the endomorphism algebra), printed pp. 47-49

items.title: The finite Hecke algebra as a convolution corner of the group algebra
items.statement: Let $G=\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$, let $B\le G$ be the upper triangular Borel and put $e_B:=|B|^{-1}\sum_{b\in B}b\in\mathbb C[G]$, an idempotent. Let $H:=e_B\,\mathbb C[G]\,e_B$, the **finite Hecke algebra** (a corner of the group algebra), with the group-algebra multiplication. Then: (1) $\mathbb C[G]e_B\cong I(1)=R_T^G(1)\cong\mathbb C[G/B]$ as left $\mathbb C[G]$-modules: the first isomorphism is the tensor/idempotent model $\mathbb C[G]e_B\cong\mathbb C[G]\otimes_{\mathbb C[B]}\widetilde 1$ and the second is the spherical identification of [[lem-spherical-principal-series-is-the-flag-permutation-module]]; (2) right multiplication $\rho_x(ye_B):=ye_Bx$ defines a $\mathbb C[G]$-equivariant endomorphism of $\mathbb C[G]e_B$, and $x\mapsto\rho_x$ is a $\mathbb C$-algebra isomorphism $$H\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C[G]}\bigl(\mathbb C[G]e_B\bigr)^{\mathrm{op}}\;\cong\;\operatorname{End}_G\bigl(\mathbb C[G/B]\bigr)^{\mathrm{op}};$$ (3) the map $w\mapsto w^{-1}$ on the standard basis defines an anti-automorphism of $H$, so $H\cong H^{\mathrm{op}}$ as abstract $\mathbb C$-algebras and the opposite in (2) is immaterial for isomorphism statements. In particular $\dim_{\mathbb C}H=|W|=n!$ and $H$ is semisimple.
items.strategy: Map $ge_B$ to the characteristic function of the coset $gB$ to identify $\mathbb C[G]e_B$ with the permutation module. For a $G$-endomorphism $f$, put $a=f(e_B)$. Then $a=e_Ba=ae_B$ and $f(ge_B)=ga$, so $f=R_a$ with $a\in H$; conversely every such right multiplication is a $G$-endomorphism. The identity $R_aR_b=R_{ba}$ gives the opposite-algebra isomorphism. Inversion $\iota(\sum c_gg)=\sum c_gg^{-1}$ is a complex-linear anti-automorphism of $\mathbb C[G]$ fixing $e_B$ and preserving $H$; it sends a double-coset basis element for $w$ to that for $w^{-1}$. This removes the opposite without assuming the later Hecke presentation. Bruhat decomposition gives dimension $n!$. Maschke makes the permutation module semisimple, and [[lem-constituent-multiplicities-under-a-semisimple-endomorphism-algebra]] makes its endomorphism algebra a finite product of complex matrix algebras; therefore $H$ is semisimple too. These arguments use only finite-dimensional linear algebra.

Ivan Losev, Lecture 8: Representations of GL_n(F_q) - Section 2.1, Lemma 2.1 (C[B\G]^B is the endomorphism algebra of C[B\G]), PDF p. 3
Charles W. Curtis, Representations of Hecke Algebras (Asterisque 168, SMF 1988) - Proposition (1.6), printed p. 15

items.title: A principal series with regular character is irreducible
items.statement: Let $\chi\in\widehat T$ be a **regular** character, i.e. its coordinates $\chi_1,\dots,\chi_n$ are pairwise distinct ([[def-diagonal-torus-characters-and-weyl-action]]). Then $W_\chi=1$, $\operatorname{End}_G(I(\chi))=\mathbb C\cdot\mathrm{id}$, and $I(\chi)$ is an irreducible $\mathbb C[G]$-module; its dimension is $[G:B]=\prod_{i=1}^n\frac{q^i-1}{q-1}$. Conversely, if $\chi$ is not regular then $W_\chi\ne1$ and $I(\chi)$ is reducible; hence $$I(\chi)\text{ is irreducible}\iff W_\chi=1\iff\chi\text{ is regular}.$$ In particular, for a fixed prime power $q$ every principal series attached to a regular character is irreducible, and its isomorphism class depends only on the $S_n$-orbit of $\chi$.
items.strategy: If $\chi$ is regular then $W_\chi=1$ and [[thm-weyl-stabilizer-controls-principal-series-endomorphisms]] gives $\dim\operatorname{End}_G(I(\chi))=1$, so $\operatorname{End}_G(I(\chi))=\mathbb C\cdot\mathrm{id}$. Since $\mathbb C[G]$ is semisimple by Maschke's theorem, $I(\chi)$ is a semisimple $\mathbb C[G]$-module, and a nonzero semisimple module whose endomorphism algebra is one-dimensional is simple: otherwise it would be a direct sum of at least two nonzero summands and the projections would give more than one linearly independent endomorphism (Schur's lemma, [[thm-schurs-lemma-for-modules]], [[thm-submodules-and-quotients-of-semisimple-modules]]). Conversely, if $W_\chi\ne1$ then $\dim\operatorname{End}_G(I(\chi))=|W_\chi|>1$; if $I(\chi)$ were simple then Schur's lemma would make $\operatorname{End}_G(I(\chi))$ a finite-dimensional division algebra over $\mathbb C$, hence $\mathbb C$, a contradiction. The dimension is the index $[G:B]$ computed in [[def-principal-series-module-for-finite-gl-n]]. No choice principle is used.

references.title: Masao Oi, Representation Theory of Finite Groups of Lie Type - Proposition 2.7 and its proof (if chi_1 != chi_2 then chi_1 x chi_2 is irreducible), printed pp. 10-11
Jay Taylor, Finite Reductive Groups - Theorem 5.21 and Example 5.22, printed pp. 45-46

items.title: The Bruhat double coset basis of the finite Hecke algebra
items.statement: Keep $G=\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$, $B$, $e_B$ and $H=e_B\mathbb C[G]e_B$. For $w\in S_n$ put $\dot w\in G$ for the permutation matrix and define the **standard basis element** $$T_w\;:=\;q^{\ell(w)}\,e_B\,\dot w\,e_B\;=\;|B|^{-1}\sum_{x\in B\dot wB}x\;\in\;H,$$ where the second equality uses $|B\dot wB|/|B|=q^{\ell(w)}$ ([[prop-cardinality-of-a-finite-bruhat-cell]]). Then: (1) $T_1=e_B$ is the unit of $H$; (2) by the Bruhat decomposition $G=\bigsqcup_{w\in S_n}B\dot wB$ ([[thm-bruhat-decomposition-of-gl-n-over-a-finite-field]]) the elements $T_w$, $w\in S_n$, are linearly independent and form a $\mathbb C$-basis of $H$; (3) under the identification of $H$ with the convolution algebra $\mathbb C[B\backslash G]^B$, $T_w$ is $|B|^{-1}\sum_{x\in B\dot wB}x$ and corresponds to the normalised characteristic function of the double coset $B\dot wB$. This is the normalization used for the rest of the page; it is the Dudas--Michel normalization in which the length-additive products are monomials and the rank-one relation reads $T_s^2=(q-1)T_s+q\,T_1$.
items.strategy: The equality $q^{\ell(w)}e_B\dot we_B=|B|^{-1}\sum_{x\in B\dot wB}x$ is the counting computation $e_B\dot we_B=|B\cap\dot w^{-1}B\dot w|\,|B|^{-2}\sum_{x\in B\dot wB}x$ with $[B:B\cap\dot w^{-1}B\dot w]=q^{\ell(w)}$; the counting stabiliser and the cell cardinality are the content of [[prop-cardinality-of-a-finite-bruhat-cell]]. Since the double cosets $B\dot wB$ are pairwise disjoint and cover $G$, the elements $|B|^{-1}\sum_{x\in B\dot wB}x$ are linearly independent in $\mathbb C[G]$, and they span $H$ because every element of $e_B\mathbb C[G]e_B$ is a linear combination of $B$-bi-invariant elements, i.e. of sums over double cosets. No choice principle is used.

references.title: Olivier Dudas and Jean Michel, Lectures on Finite Reductive Groups and Their Representations - Section 11.1, the basis (T_w) with T_w = q^{l(w)} e_{B^F} w e_{B^F}, printed p. 46
Jay Taylor, Finite Reductive Groups - Section 5, the standard basis T_w of H(G,B) = e C[G] e, printed pp. 44-45

items.title: Principal series endomorphisms as an idempotent corner
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $q$ be a prime power, put $G=\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$
with Borel $B=T\ltimes U$, let $\chi\in\widehat T$ with inflation
$\widetilde\chi$ to $B$, and let
$$e_\chi:=\frac{1}{|B|}\sum_{b\in B}\widetilde\chi(b)^{-1}b\;\in\;\mathbb C[B]\subseteq\mathbb C[G],$$
the idempotent of the one-dimensional representation $\widetilde\chi$ of $B$,
so that $be_\chi=e_\chi b=\widetilde\chi(b)e_\chi$ for $b\in B$. Then:

1. the map
$\mathbb C[G]e_\chi\to I(\chi)$, $ge_\chi\mapsto f_g$, where
$f_g(gb)=\widetilde\chi(b)^{-1}$ and $f_g=0$ outside $gB$, is an isomorphism
of left $\mathbb C[G]$-modules;
2. right multiplication defines an algebra isomorphism
$$e_\chi\mathbb C[G]e_\chi\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C[G]}\bigl(\mathbb C[G]e_\chi\bigr)^{\mathrm{op}}\;\cong\;\operatorname{End}_G\bigl(I(\chi)\bigr)^{\mathrm{op}};$$
3. writing $\dot w$ for the permutation matrix of $w\in S_n$, the elements
$e_\chi\dot we_\chi$, $w\in S_n$, span $e_\chi\mathbb C[G]e_\chi$; one has
$e_\chi\dot we_\chi=0$ whenever $w\notin W_\chi$, and the elements
$e_\chi\dot we_\chi$ with $w\in W_\chi$ form a $\mathbb C$-basis of
$e_\chi\mathbb C[G]e_\chi$. Hence
$\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{End}_G(I(\chi))=|W_\chi|$, with basis indexed by
the Weyl stabiliser, in accordance with
thm-weyl-stabilizer-controls-principal-series-endomorphisms.

No choice principle is used beyond the finite selection of coset
representatives used to exhibit a basis.
items.strategy: The covariance functions $f_g$ satisfy $f_{gb}=\widetilde\chi(b)f_g$, exactly the relation $gbe_\chi=\widetilde\chi(b)ge_\chi$; both models have the basis indexed by a finite left transversal, proving (1). Right multiplication $R_a$ satisfies $R_aR_b=R_{ba}$, giving the stated opposite-algebra identification. Bruhat decomposition and $e_\chi b=be_\chi=\widetilde\chi(b)e_\chi$ show spanning by $e_\chi\dot we_\chi$. For $t\in T$, the identities $e_\chi t\dot we_\chi=\chi(t)e_\chi\dot we_\chi=\chi(\dot w^{-1}t\dot w)e_\chi\dot we_\chi$ force vanishing unless $w\cdot\chi=\chi$. At most $|W_\chi|$ spanning vectors remain, and the dimension theorem [[thm-weyl-stabilizer-controls-principal-series-endomorphisms]] gives exactly that dimension, so all these vectors are nonzero and independent.

references.title: Ivan Losev, Lecture 8: Representations of GL_n(F_q) - Section 2.1, Lemma 2.1 and its proof (the idempotent corner e C[B\G] e), PDF pp. 3-4
Olivier Dudas and Jean Michel, Lectures on Finite Reductive Groups and Their Representations - Section 11.1 (the corner H = e_{B^F} Lambda G^F e_{B^F}), printed p. 46

items.title: Length-additive products in the finite Hecke algebra
items.statement: Let $T_w$ be the standard basis of $H=e_B\mathbb C[G]e_B$ and let $\ell$ be the inversion length on $S_n$. Then for all $u,v\in S_n$ with $\ell(uv)=\ell(u)+\ell(v)$ one has $$T_uT_v=T_{uv}.$$ In particular $T_wT_{s_i}=T_{ws_i}$ whenever $\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)+1$, and by induction on a reduced expression $T_w=T_{s_{i_1}}\cdots T_{s_{i_\ell}}$ for every reduced word $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_\ell}$. The same statement holds with the product in the other order, $T_vT_u=T_{vu}$ when $\ell(vu)=\ell(v)+\ell(u)$.
items.strategy: Write $T_u=|B|^{-1}\sum_{x\in B\dot uB}x$ and $T_v=|B|^{-1}\sum_{y\in B\dot vB}y$; then $T_uT_v=|B|^{-2}\sum_{x,y}xy$. For $\ell(uv)=\ell(u)+\ell(v)$ the product set satisfies $B\dot uB\cdot B\dot vB=B\dot u\dot vB$: the inclusion $\subseteq$ is the standard Bruhat exchange computation and the reverse inclusion with the cardinality identity $|B\dot uB|\,|B\dot vB|=|B\dot u\dot vB|\,|B|$ follows from $|B\dot wB|=q^{\ell(w)}|B|$ ([[prop-cardinality-of-a-finite-bruhat-cell]]). The group $B$ acts freely on $B\dot uB\times B\dot vB$ by $b\cdot(x,y):=(xb^{-1},by)$, and the product is invariant under this action, so every $\mu$-fiber is a union of free $B$-orbits; the source has $|B\dot uB|\,|B\dot vB|/|B|=q^{\ell(u)+\ell(v)}|B|=|B\dot u\dot vB|$ orbits and $\mu$ maps them onto $B\dot u\dot vB$, so this surjection between finite sets of equal cardinality is a bijection: every fiber is a single free orbit of size $|B|$ and $\sum_{x,y}xy=|B|\sum_{z\in B\dot u\dot vB}z$, whence $T_uT_v=|B|^{-1}\sum_z z=T_{uv}$. The right-handed statement follows by applying the same computation to $\dot v\dot u$ or by symmetry. No choice principle is used.

references.title: Olivier Dudas and Jean Michel, Lectures on Finite Reductive Groups and Their Representations - Equation (11.1), printed p. 46
Ivan Losev, Lecture 8: Representations of GL_n(F_q) - Proposition 2.3, first case, PDF p. 4
Jay Taylor, Finite Reductive Groups - The first relation for $\bar T_s\bar T_w$, printed p. 44

items.title: The rank-one quadratic relation in the finite Hecke algebra
items.statement: For every simple reflection $s=s_i\in S_n$ the standard basis element $T_s\in H$ satisfies $$T_s^2=(q-1)T_s+q\,T_1,$$ equivalently $(T_s-q)(T_s+1)=0$; here $T_1=e_B$ is the unit. Consequently the two eigenvalues of $T_s$ in any finite-dimensional representation of $H$ lie among $q$ and $-1$.
items.strategy: Let $\mu:B\dot sB\times B\dot sB\to G$ be the multiplication map and $U_s:=B\dot sB$. The group $B$ acts freely on $U_s\times U_s$ by $b\cdot(x,y):=(xb^{-1},by)$ and the product is invariant under this action, so the fibers of $\mu$ are unions of free $B$-orbits; the number $m(g):=|\mu^{-1}(g)|/|B|$ of orbits over $g$ is constant on $(B,B)$-double cosets, because $(x,y)\mapsto(bx,yb')$ is a $B$-equivariant bijection $\mu^{-1}(g)\to\mu^{-1}(bgb')$. The image of $\mu$ is $B\dot sB\cdot B\dot sB\subseteq B\dot sB\cup B$ (the Bruhat exchange computation), so the two constants $m_1:=m(1)$ and $m_2:=m(s)$ control the product. Counting the source, $|U_s|^2=q^2|B|^2=m_1|B|\cdot|B|+m_2|B|\cdot|U_s|=m_1|B|^2+m_2q|B|^2$, i.e. $q^2=m_1+qm_2$; and $\mu^{-1}(1)\cong U_s$ (via $x\mapsto(x,x^{-1})$ after fixing a representative), so $m_1=q$ and hence $m_2=q-1$. Therefore $T_s^2=|B|^{-2}\sum_{x,y}xy=|B|^{-1}\bigl(q\sum_{g\in B}g+(q-1)\sum_{g\in U_s}g\bigr)=q\,e_B+(q-1)T_s=(q-1)T_s+q\,T_1$, which is the displayed relation. Equivalently, Dudas--Michel compute $(e_B\dot se_B)^2=\frac{q-1}{q}e_B\dot se_B+\frac1qe_B$ directly; multiplying by $q^2$ and using $T_s=qe_B\dot se_B$ gives the same identity. No choice principle is used.

references.title: Olivier Dudas and Jean Michel, Lectures on Finite Reductive Groups and Their Representations - Equation (11.2) and the preceding computation of $(e_{B^F}se_{B^F})^2$, printed p. 46
Ivan Losev, Lecture 8: Representations of GL_n(F_q) - Proposition 2.3, second half ($T_s^2=q+(q-1)T_s$), PDF p. 4
Jay Taylor, Finite Reductive Groups - The second relation for $\bar T_s\bar T_w$ with $q_s=[B:\dot sB\dot s^{-1}\cap B]$, printed p. 44
Charles W. Curtis, Representations of Hecke Algebras (Asterisque 168) - Theorem (1.6) and the Iwahori-Matsumoto proof (the parameters $q_i=[B:\dot s_iB\cap B]$), printed pp. 18-19

items.title: The finite spherical Hecke algebra is semisimple with nondegenerate trace form
items.statement: The finite Hecke algebra $H=e_B\mathbb C[G]e_B$ of $G=\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$ is a semisimple finite-dimensional $\mathbb C$-algebra of dimension $n!$, and its trace form $(x,y)\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(L_{xy})$ is nondegenerate. Consequently $H$ is isomorphic to a product of matrix algebras and its simple modules form a complete set of invariants of its semisimple representations.
items.strategy: $H$ is the corner $e_B\mathbb C[G]e_B$ of the group algebra of the finite group $G$ at the idempotent $e_B$; $\mathbb C[G]$ is semisimple by Maschke's theorem, and a corner of a semisimple finite-dimensional algebra at an idempotent is semisimple (its modules are direct summands of modules for the ambient algebra). Nondegeneracy of the trace form is then the general characterization [[lem-trace-form-nondegeneracy-characterizes-semisimple-finite-dimensional-algebras]]. The dimension is $n!$ by [[def-bruhat-double-coset-basis-of-the-finite-hecke-algebra]]. No choice principle is used.

references.title: Ivan Losev, Lecture 8: Representations of GL_n(F_q) - Section 2.1: 'this algebra is manifestly semisimple'; Section 2.3, semisimplicity of $H_{\mathbb C,q}(n)$, PDF pp. 4-5
Jay Taylor, Finite Reductive Groups - Proposition 5.16 ($H_1\cong\mathbb C W^F$ and $H_q\cong H(G,B)$ are both semisimple), printed pp. 44-45
Olivier Dudas and Jean Michel, Lectures on Finite Reductive Groups and Their Representations - Section 11.1 (the corner of the semisimple group algebra), printed pp. 45-46

items.title: Standard intertwining operators for the finite principal series
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $q$ be a prime power, put $G=\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$
with upper triangular Borel $B$, diagonal torus $T$ and unipotent radical $U$,
let $W=S_n$ be the Weyl group with inversion length $\ell$ and canonical
permutation matrix $\dot w$ for $w\in W$
(def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n), let $\chi\in\widehat T$ be a
character with Weyl stabiliser $W_\chi=\{w\in W:w\cdot\chi=\chi\}$
(def-diagonal-torus-characters-and-weyl-action), and let
$$e_\chi=\frac{1}{|B|}\sum_{b\in B}\widetilde\chi(b)^{-1}b$$
be the idempotent of $\widetilde\chi$ in the corner
$e_\chi\mathbb C[G]e_\chi$, whose elements
$e_\chi\dot we_\chi$, $w\in W_\chi$, form a $\mathbb C$-basis, with
$\mathbb C[G]e_\chi\cong I(\chi)$ as left $\mathbb C[G]$-modules
(lem-principal-series-endomorphisms-as-the-chi-idempotent-corner,
def-principal-series-module-for-finite-gl-n).

For $w\in W_\chi$ put
$$\Theta_w\;:=\;q^{\ell(w)}\,e_\chi\dot w\,e_\chi\;\in\;e_\chi\mathbb C[G]e_\chi,$$
the normalization by $q^{\ell(w)}$ being the one of the Bruhat double-coset
basis of the finite Hecke algebra
(def-bruhat-double-coset-basis-of-the-finite-hecke-algebra), where
$|B\dot wB|/|B|=q^{\ell(w)}$
(prop-cardinality-of-a-finite-bruhat-cell). The **standard intertwining
operator** attached to $w\in W_\chi$ is the endomorphism
$$B_w\;:=\;R_{\Theta_{w^{-1}}}\;\in\;\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C[G]}\bigl(\mathbb C[G]e_\chi\bigr)\;\cong\;\operatorname{End}_G\bigl(I(\chi)\bigr),$$
where $R_a(xe_\chi):=xe_\chi a$ is right multiplication by $a$, the operators
being transported to $\operatorname{End}_G(I(\chi))$ along the isomorphism of
lem-principal-series-endomorphisms-as-the-chi-idempotent-corner. The index
$w^{-1}$ is forced by the reversal of composition in the identification of the
endomorphism algebra with the opposite of the corner: $R_aR_b=R_{ba}$. In
particular $\Theta_1=q^0e_\chi=e_\chi$ and $B_1=\mathrm{id}$, and since
$\Theta_w$, $w\in W_\chi$, is a $\mathbb C$-basis of the corner, the operators
$B_w$, $w\in W_\chi$, form a $\mathbb C$-basis of
$\operatorname{End}_G(I(\chi))$.

**Representative independence.** Let $w\in W_\chi$ and $g=b_1\dot wb_2$ with
$b_1,b_2\in B$. Because $e_\chi b=\widetilde\chi(b)e_\chi$ for $b\in B$ one has
$$e_\chi ge_\chi=\widetilde\chi(b_1)\widetilde\chi(b_2)\,e_\chi\dot we_\chi,$$
so the compensated element
$\widetilde\chi(b_1)^{-1}\widetilde\chi(b_2)^{-1}e_\chi ge_\chi$ equals
$e_\chi\dot we_\chi$. If $g=b_1'\dot wb_2'$ is a second decomposition, the two
compensated elements agree: comparing the decompositions gives
$b_1^{-1}b_1'=\dot w\,b_2b_2'^{-1}\dot w^{-1}\in B$, and
$\widetilde\chi(b_1^{-1}b_1')=\widetilde\chi(b_2b_2'^{-1})$, so
$\widetilde\chi(b_1)\widetilde\chi(b_2)=\widetilde\chi(b_1')\widetilde\chi(b_2')$.
The same computation shows that the characteristic function of the coset
$tB$, $t\in T$, is hit with the torus factor
$\widetilde\chi(t)=\chi(t)$: if $n_w=t\dot w$ with $t\in T$, then
$$\chi(t)^{-1}e_\chi n_we_\chi=e_\chi\dot we_\chi,$$
the special case $b_1=t$, $b_2=1$ displayed in the normalization. Thus the
compensated corner element, and hence $B_w$, is independent of the choice of
double-coset representatives; the uncompensated element $e_\chi ge_\chi$
generally is not. This is the one-dimensional case of the simultaneous
representative and $\gamma_n$ convention of Dudas-Michel, Section 11.3.

**Remarks on indexing.** For $\chi=1$ this is the usual spherical basis with
inverse index in the endomorphism model. Raw basis elements for characters that
have not been sorted out by the Weyl stabiliser use the ambient length
$\ell(w)$ of the permutation matrix; the Hecke-algebra basis after Weyl sorting
is specified later in this page. All constructions use finite sums, the explicit
permutation matrices $\dot w$ and the fixed idempotent $e_\chi$, so no choice
principle is used.
items.strategy: Apply the corner basis lemma and right multiplication with inverse index. A torus factor multiplies the corner element by its character value, so compensate it rather than pretending it disappears. For a general double-coset representative, character covariance gives the displayed factor; two decompositions differ by an element of the Borel intersection, where the two inflated characters agree. This is the one-dimensional version of the simultaneous representative and $\gamma_n$ convention in Dudas--Michel §11.3. These are finite sums and use no choice principle.

items.title: The type-A Iwahori-Hecke presentation of the finite Hecke algebra
items.statement: Let $G=\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$, $H=e_B\mathbb C[G]e_B$ and $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}\in H$ the standard basis elements attached to the simple transpositions. Then: (1) $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ generate $H$; (2) they satisfy $$T_i^2=(q-1)T_i+q\,T_1,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1}\quad(1\le i\le n-2),\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(|i-j|>1);$$ (3) these relations present $H$: if $H(n):=\mathbb C\langle T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}\rangle/(\text{the three families of relations})$ is the abstract $\mathbb C$-algebra with generators and relations displayed in (2), then the natural map $H(n)\to H$, $T_i\mapsto T_i$, is an isomorphism. Equivalently, $H$ is the specialization at $v=q$ of the generic type-A Hecke algebra: $H\cong\mathbb C\otimes_{\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]}H_v(n)$ under $v\mapsto q$. In particular $H$ has dimension $n!$ and the images of the standard basis $T_w$ form a basis.
items.strategy: (1) and (2): the length-increasing rule ([[lem-length-increasing-hecke-products]]) identifies $T_w$ with a product of simple generators along a reduced word, so the $T_i$ generate $H$; the quadratic relation is [[lem-rank-one-hecke-quadratic-relation]]; the commutation and adjacent braid relations are checked by expanding the two sides in the basis $\{T_w\}$ using the length rules (for the braid relation all terms lie in the span of $T_1,T_{s_i},T_{s_{i+1}},T_{s_is_{i+1}},T_{s_{i+1}s_i},T_{s_is_{i+1}s_i}$ and the two expansions agree because the reduced words $s_is_{i+1}s_i$ and $s_{i+1}s_is_{i+1}$ define the same $T_w$ by Matsumoto, [[lem-type-a-reduced-words-are-connected-by-braid-moves]]). (3): the abstract algebra $H(n)$ is spanned by the products $T_{i_1}\cdots T_{i_k}$ over all words; using the relations those can be rewritten as linear combinations of $T_w$ for $w\in S_n$ (reduced-word rewriting; well-definedness of $T_w$ is the same Matsumoto lemma and the Coxeter presentation of $S_n$, [[thm-the-symmetric-group-has-the-coxeter-presentation]]), so $\dim_{\mathbb C}H(n)\le n!$; the natural map $H(n)\to H$ is well defined and surjective by (1)-(2), while $\dim_{\mathbb C}H=n!$ by the standard basis, so it is an isomorphism. The identification with the specialization at $v=q$ follows because the defining relations of $H_v(n)$ specialize exactly to the relations (2). No choice principle is used; all dimensions are finite.

items.title: The standard intertwiners form a basis of the principal series endomorphism algebra
items.statement:
The canonical, compensated operators $B_w$ defined in
def-standard-intertwining-operators-for-finite-principal-series,
$w\in W_\chi$, form a $\mathbb C$-basis of
$\operatorname{End}_G I(\chi)$. Their dimension is $|W_\chi|$. For two
characters, the analogous corner between their idempotents, with the covariance
compensation and the opposite orientation matched to its source and target,
gives a Hom basis indexed by $\{w:\chi=w\cdot\chi'\}$. No choice principle is
used.
items.strategy: The corner lemma [[lem-principal-series-endomorphisms-as-the-chi-idempotent-corner]] proves the basis: inverse indexing permutes $W_\chi$ and right multiplication is a vector-space isomorphism. For Hom spaces, Bruhat decomposition gives spanning by the corresponding mixed-corner elements, torus covariance kills precisely the unsupported indices, and [[lem-mackey-support-for-homs-between-finite-principal-series]] supplies exactly the number of remaining indices. Hence these elements are nonzero and independent. Independence of representatives means the compensated convention, not independence of an uncompensated $e_\chi n_we_\chi$.

items.title: The equal-coordinate rank-one principal series of GL_2
items.statement:
Let $M=\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_q)$ with Borel $B_2=T_2\ltimes U_2$, and
let $\chi=(a,a)$ be the character of the diagonal torus with equal coordinates,
$a$ a character of $\mathbb F_q^\times$
(def-diagonal-torus-characters-and-weyl-action). Then the principal series
$I(\chi)=\operatorname{Ind}_{B_2}^{M}(\widetilde\chi)$
(def-principal-series-module-for-finite-gl-n) has dimension $q+1$ and
splits as a direct sum of exactly two non-isomorphic simple $M$-modules,
$$I(\chi)\;\cong\;\bigl(a\circ\det\bigr)\;\oplus\;\bigl(\operatorname{St}\otimes(a\circ\det)\bigr),$$
where $a\circ\det$ is the unique one-dimensional constituent (equivalently, the
unique constituent on which $M$ acts by a character) and
$\operatorname{St}$ is the Steinberg representation of
$\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_q)$, of dimension $q$; here $\operatorname{St}$
is defined as the nontrivial simple constituent of $I(1)$, equivalently the
$M$-stable complement of the constant functions in
$I(1)\cong\mathbb C[\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_q)]$. Each constituent has multiplicity
one in $I(\chi)$ and
$\operatorname{End}_M(I(\chi))\cong\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$. In the spherical
case $a=1$ the one-dimensional constituent is the trivial representation; it
contains the $B_2$-fixed constant function on
$M/B_2\cong\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_q)$, and the standard intertwiner $B_s$ acts on
it by the scalar $q$ and on $\operatorname{St}$ by the scalar $-1$, so
$B_s^2=(q-1)B_s+q\,\mathrm{id}_{I(\chi)}$. For $a\ne1$, $I(\chi)$ has no nonzero
$B_2$-fixed vector. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy:
For $\chi_1=\chi_2=a$ the Mackey computation of Oi, Propositions 2.7--2.8, gives $\operatorname{End}_M(\chi	imes\chi)\cong\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$; by Maschke $I(\chi)$ is semisimple, and a commutative two-dimensional endomorphism algebra forces exactly two pairwise non-isomorphic constituents of multiplicity one (a constituent of multiplicity $m\ge2$ would contribute a non-commutative matrix factor $\operatorname M_m(\mathbb C)$). Oi's isomorphism $\chi	imes\chi\cong(1	imes1)\otimes(a\circ\det)$ gives the displayed splitting with $\operatorname{St}$ the $q$-dimensional constituent of $1	imes1$, and $\dim(\operatorname{St}\otimes(a\circ\det))=q\ge2$ identifies $a\circ\det$ as the unique one-dimensional constituent. $B_2$-fixed vectors: for $a=1$ the constant function on $M/B_2$ is fixed by $B_2$ and spans the trivial constituent; for $a
e1$ the equal-coordinate case of Oi's Mackey decomposition gives $\operatorname{Res}_{B_2}^M I(\chi)\cong\widetilde\chi\oplus\operatorname{Ind}_{T}^{B_2}(\widetilde\chi)$, whence $\operatorname{Hom}_{B_2}(\mathbf 1,I(\chi))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{B_2}(\mathbf 1,\widetilde\chi)\oplus\operatorname{Hom}_T(\mathbf 1,\widetilde\chi)=0$ because $\widetilde\chi
e1$; so there is no nonzero $B_2$-fixed vector for $a
e1$ (the $B_2$-fixed space is not one-dimensional when $a=1$ either: it is $2$-dimensional, spanned by the constants and by the indicator of the open cell). Eigenvalues for $a=1$: under [[def-standard-intertwining-operators-for-finite-principal-series]] the operator $B_s$ is right multiplication by $T_s=q\,e_{B_2}\dot se_{B_2}$ on $\mathbb C[M]e_{B_2}=I(1)$ ([[def-bruhat-double-coset-basis-of-the-finite-hecke-algebra]], [[thm-finite-hecke-algebra-as-convolution-corner-and-endomorphisms]]); the $G$-invariant vector is $\sum_{g\in M}g=|M|e_{\mathrm{triv}}$ with $e_{\mathrm{triv}}e_{B_2}=e_{\mathrm{triv}}$, so $B_s\cdot e_{\mathrm{triv}}=q\,e_{\mathrm{triv}}$ and the scalar on the trivial constituent is $q$. Since $T_s$ satisfies $T_s^2=(q-1)T_s+q$ in $H$ ([[lem-rank-one-hecke-quadratic-relation]]), the scalar on the other constituent lies in $\{q,-1\}$, and it is not $q$ again: otherwise $B_s-q$ would annihilate both constituents while $B_s
e q\cdot\mathrm{id}$ ($B_s\cdot e_{B_2}=q\,e_{B_2}\dot se_{B_2}
otin\mathbb C e_{B_2}$); hence it is $-1$. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Group algebra and finite-field specializations of the generic Hecke algebra
items.statement: Let $H_v(n)$ be the generic type-A Hecke algebra over $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ and let $q$ be a prime power. (1) The specialization $v\mapsto1$ is an isomorphism of $\mathbb C$-algebras $$\mathbb C\otimes_{A,\,v\mapsto1}H_v(n)\;\cong\;\mathbb C[S_n],$$ carrying $T_w$ to $w$; (2) the specialization $v\mapsto q$ is an isomorphism of $\mathbb C$-algebras $$\mathbb C\otimes_{A,\,v\mapsto q}H_v(n)\;\cong\;H=e_B\mathbb C[G]e_B,\qquad G=\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q),$$ carrying the generic generator $T_i$ to the standard basis element $T_{s_i}$; (3) both specializations are semisimple $\mathbb C$-algebras, and the isomorphisms are compatible with the standard bases ($\{T_w\}$ in each case).
items.strategy: (1) At $v=1$ the relations of $H_v(n)$ become $T_i^2=1$ together with the braid and commutation relations, i.e. the Coxeter presentation of $S_n$ ([[thm-the-symmetric-group-has-the-coxeter-presentation]]); hence the specialization is $\mathbb C[S_n]$ by the universal property, and $\dim=n!$. (2) At $v=q$ the relations become those of [[thm-type-a-iwahori-hecke-presentation]], which presents $H$ with the same generators; the resulting algebra homomorphism is surjective and both sides have dimension $n!$ (for $H$, the Bruhat basis), hence an isomorphism. (3) $\mathbb C[S_n]$ is semisimple by Maschke and $H$ is semisimple by [[lem-semisimplicity-and-trace-form-for-the-finite-spherical-hecke-algebra]]. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Length-additive products of the standard intertwiners
items.statement:
For Weyl-sorted $\eta=(a_1^{n_1},\dots,a_k^{n_k})$ with distinct $a_r$, put
$L=\prod_r\operatorname{GL}_{n_r}(\mathbb F_q)$ and
$\rho(l)=\prod_r a_r(\det l_r)$. With the canonical intertwiners $B_w$ of
def-standard-intertwining-operators-for-finite-principal-series, set
$T_w=\rho(\dot w)^{-1}B_w$ for $w\in W_\eta$. Then $T_uT_v=T_{uv}$ whenever the
intrinsic (equivalently here ambient) lengths add, and the simple $T_s$ satisfy
all type-A braid and commuting relations. The raw basis also has length-additive
products $B_uB_v=B_{uv}$ in these sorted coordinates. For arbitrary $\chi$,
choose the prescribed sorting $\eta$ and a module isomorphism
$J:I(\chi)\to I(\eta)$ from
thm-weyl-stabilizer-controls-principal-series-endomorphisms; transport the
normalized basis through $J$. Its labels and length are transported through the
sorting permutation. This does not identify the unsorted raw ambient-length
basis with the transported basis. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: The principal series in $L$ is the tensor product of spherical principal series in its factors twisted by $\rho$, since $\rho|_{B\cap L}=\eta$. The algebra automorphism $g\mapsto\rho(g)g$ sends $e_\eta$ to $e_{B\cap L}$ and $q^{\ell(w)}e_\eta\dot we_\eta$ to $\rho(\dot w)q^{\ell(w)}e_{B\cap L}\dot we_{B\cap L}$. Right multiplication with inverse labels transfers the spherical length-additive products and braid relations to the $T_w$. Here $\rho(\dot w)=\prod_r a_r(-1)^{\ell(w_r)}\in\{1,-1\}$ and is a group character, so it also transfers the length-additive products to $B_w$. Harish--Chandra induction from $L$ to $G$ preserves these operator identities and identifies $R_L^G I_L(\eta)$ with $I_G(\eta)$ by [[thm-transitivity-and-parabolic-independence-of-harish-chandra-induction]]. The induced operators are exactly the displayed $B_w$: writing $e_\eta^G=e_{U_P}e_\eta^L$ and observing that $L$ normalizes $U_P$ gives $e_\eta^G\dot we_\eta^G=e_{U_P}e_\eta^L\dot we_\eta^L$. Finally conjugating all operators by $J$ preserves every product. There is no inference of braid relations merely from the corresponding permutation identities.

items.title: Tits deformation for the type-A Hecke algebra
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X=D(f)\subseteq\mathbb A^1_{\mathbb C}$ be a
nonempty principal open, let $A$ be a unital associative
$\mathbb C[z,1/f]$-algebra free of finite rank, and let $x,y\in X$ have
semisimple fibers. Then $A_x\cong A_y$ as $\mathbb C$-algebras. In particular,
for every prime power $q$,
$$H_q(S_n)\cong e_B\mathbb C[\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)]e_B\cong\mathbb C[S_n],$$
preserving the number and dimensions of simple modules. AC is used through the
published Chevalley constructibility and strong Nullstellensatz suppliers, not
in the formal lifting or determinant argument.
items.strategy: If the rank is zero all fibers are the zero algebra. Otherwise fix a free basis and write its multiplication coefficients as rational functions in $z$ with denominators powers of $f$. The trace-form determinant is regular; write $\Delta(z)=d(z)/f(z)^m$ with $d\in\mathbb C[z]$. [[lem-trace-form-nondegeneracy-characterizes-semisimple-finite-dimensional-algebras]] makes $Y=D(fd)$ exactly the semisimple locus, containing $x,y$. This is a nonempty principal open of the line. At $x$, the homomorphism $\mathbb C[z,1/(f\Delta)]\to R=\mathbb C[\![t]\!]$ sends $z$ to $x+t$; the denominator is a unit because its constant term is nonzero. The completion is explicitly $R$: modulo $(z-x)^m$, localization of the denominator does nothing because it is already a unit, so the inverse limit is the compatible truncated power-series ring. Base change gives a free complete algebra reducing to $A_x$. By [[lem-formal-triviality-of-one-parameter-semisimple-algebras]] it is isomorphic to $R\otimes_\mathbb C A_x$, providing a matrix $P(t)$ with unit determinant satisfying all multiplication-preservation equations. To pass from formal solutions to classical fibers, define the affine incidence algebraic set $Z_x$ of $(z,P,h,u)$ by those equations after clearing denominators and by $h\det P=1$ and $u(fd)(z)=1$. The projection to $Y$ is a classical morphism by [[def-classical-affine-variety-morphism]]; its image $E_x$ is exactly the locus of fibers isomorphic to $A_x$. By [[thm-chevalley-constructible-image-varieties]] it is constructible (this supplier explicitly assumes AC). If $E_x$ were finite, the nonzero polynomial $g(z)=\prod_{a\in E_x}(z-a)$ would vanish on every complex point of $Z_x$. [[thm-affine-nullstellensatz-correspondence]], specifically $I(V(J))=\sqrt J$ (under AC), would give $g^N$ in the ideal defining $Z_x$. But the formal isomorphism, together with $h(t)=(\det P(t))^{-1}$ and $u(t)=(fd)(x+t)^{-1}$, is a solution of these equations in $\mathbb C[\![t]\!]$. Substitution would imply $g(x+t)^N=0$, impossible in the power-series domain for a nonzero polynomial. Thus $E_x$ is infinite. A constructible subset of a principal open of the line is finite or cofinite: every proper closed subset is finite, so in a finite union of locally closed pieces an infinite piece must contain a nonempty open, whose complement is finite. Hence $E_x$ is cofinite in $Y$. Repeat at $y$; the two cofinite sets meet because $Y$ is infinite. A fiber at a point of their intersection is isomorphic to both $A_x,A_y$, proving the theorem. This fills Losev's formal-to-Zariski step without claiming that an object-only coordinate-duality theorem proves morphism facts, or that formal triviality alone proves an orbit preimage open. Finally apply this to the free standard-basis algebra $\mathbb C[v^{\pm1}]\otimes H_v(n)$ at $1,q$, whose fibers are semisimple by [[prop-group-algebra-and-finite-field-specializations-of-the-generic-hecke-algebra]] and [[lem-semisimplicity-and-trace-form-for-the-finite-spherical-hecke-algebra]].

items.title: The rank-one Hecke parameter for equal torus characters
items.statement:
For Weyl-sorted $\eta$, each simple $s\in S_\eta$ exchanges two adjacent equal
coordinates $a,a$. The associated rank-one Levi has principal series
$(a\circ\det)\oplus(\operatorname{St}\otimes a\circ\det)$ on its
$\operatorname{GL}_2$ factor, tensored with one-dimensional characters on the
remaining torus factors, with constituent degrees $1,q$. The canonical raw
intertwiner has eigenvalues $a(-1)q$ and $-a(-1)$. The normalized
$T_s=a(-1)^{-1}B_s$ satisfies $T_s^2=(q-1)T_s+q\,\mathrm{id}$; thus the
parameter is exactly $q$, and the normalization of
lem-length-additive-products-of-standard-intertwiners gives
$\lambda_w=\prod_r a_r(-1)^{-\ell(w_r)}$. For arbitrary $\chi$ this assertion
holds for the transported generators after Weyl sorting. In particular the naive
generator fails the parameter-$q$ relation when $a(-1)=-1$: for $q=3$ and the
nontrivial character of $\mathbb F_3^\times$, its eigenvalue on $a\circ\det$ is
$-3$, which is neither $3$ nor $-1$. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Use the determinant twist in [[lem-length-additive-products-of-standard-intertwiners]] on the rank-one Levi. The twist sends the raw corner generator to $a(\det\dot s)T_s^{\mathrm{sph}}=a(-1)T_s^{\mathrm{sph}}$, and the spherical quadratic relation gives exactly the eigenvalues $a(-1)q,-a(-1)$ and their rescaling. The equal-character splitting and degrees are [[lem-equal-coordinate-rank-one-principal-series-of-gl2-fq]]. Harish--Chandra induction preserves the quadratic polynomial identity, and sorting transports it to all characters. This explicitly computes the normalization and does not use an unread formula for the quotient of constituent degrees; Dudas--Michel Theorem 11.11 provides an independent structural cross-check only.

items.title: The finite Hecke algebra is non-canonically isomorphic to the group algebra of S_n
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, used through Tits deformation. For every prime power
$q$ there is an isomorphism of $\mathbb C$-algebras
$H=e_B\mathbb C[G]e_B\cong\mathbb C[S_n]$,
$G=\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$, and no isomorphism sending every standard
basis element $T_w$ to $w$ exists for $n\ge2$ and $q\ne1$, since their quadratic
relations differ: the deformation isomorphism is not canonical, does not
identify the natural bases, and need not identify the simple modules of $H$ with
those of $\mathbb C[S_n]$ in any prescribed way. Consequently $H$ and
$\mathbb C[S_n]$ have the same number of simple modules and the same multiset of
dimensions of simple modules, but no natural bijection of simple modules is
asserted.
items.strategy: Immediate from [[thm-tits-deformation-for-the-type-a-hecke-algebra]] applied to $A=\mathbb C[v^{\pm1}]\otimes H_v(n)$ at the two points $1$ and $q$; the non-canonicity is the content of Taylor's Remark 5.23 and of the fact that the deformation isomorphism is produced by an formal lifting and constructible incidence argument, neither of which selects a basis or a bijection of simple modules. The Axiom of Choice is carried from the Tits-deformation supplier; all remaining steps are finite-dimensional.

items.title: The endomorphism algebra of a general finite principal series
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, used for the Tits-deformation conclusion below. Let $\chi$ be any torus character of $G=\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$, with equal-character block sizes $n_1,\ldots,n_k$ and stabilizer $W_\chi\cong\prod_rS_{n_r}$. Then $\operatorname{End}_G I(\chi)\cong\bigotimes_r H_q(S_{n_r})=H_q(W_\chi)$, with every parameter exactly $q$. In Weyl-sorted coordinates $\eta=(a_1^{n_1},\ldots,a_k^{n_k})$ the Hecke basis maps to $T_w=\lambda_wB_w$, where $\lambda_w=\prod_r a_r(-1)^{-\ell(w_r)}$ and $B_w$ uses right multiplication with inverse indexing. For an unsorted character the Hecke basis is transported from this sorted module through a module isomorphism; this statement makes no equality claim between that transported basis and the raw ambient-length Bruhat basis. Consequently $\operatorname{End}_G I(\chi)$ is semisimple and is abstractly isomorphic to $\mathbb C[W_\chi]$, preserving simple-module dimensions. Characters in the same $S_n$-orbit give isomorphic principal-series modules and endomorphism algebras. The endomorphism algebra identification with $H_q(W_\chi)$ itself uses no choice principle.
items.strategy: First sort the coordinates as in [[def-diagonal-torus-characters-and-weyl-action]], using the Weyl-orbit module isomorphism [[thm-weyl-stabilizer-controls-principal-series-endomorphisms]]. For sorted $\eta$, let $L=\prod_r\operatorname{GL}_{n_r}$, $P=L\ltimes U_P$ and $M=I_L(\eta)$. Transitivity identifies $R_L^GM=I_G(\eta)$. Inflation and induction give a unital algebra homomorphism $\operatorname{End}_L M\to\operatorname{End}_G R_L^GM$. It is injective: if $f(v)\ne0$, the induced function supported on $P$ with value $v$ at $1$ is sent to one whose value at $1$ is $f(v)\ne0$. Determinant twisting identifies $\operatorname{End}_L M$ with the tensor product of the spherical endomorphism algebras; [[thm-type-a-iwahori-hecke-presentation]] identifies these with $H_q(S_{n_r})$, using inverse indexing to remove the opposite. Its dimension is $\prod_r n_r!$ by the standard basis. The Mackey dimension theorem gives the same dimension for $\operatorname{End}_G I_G(\eta)$, so the injection is onto. The exact normalized basis and all relations follow from [[lem-length-additive-products-of-standard-intertwiners]] and [[lem-rank-one-hecke-parameter-for-equal-torus-characters]], including the explicit $\lambda_w$. Conjugating by the sorting module isomorphism proves the full arbitrary-character assertion. Finally [[thm-tits-deformation-for-the-type-a-hecke-algebra]], under AC, identifies each factor with $\mathbb C[S_{n_r}]$; tensoring gives $\mathbb C[W_\chi]$. Semisimplicity also follows directly from Maschke and the finite semisimple-module endomorphism lemma. This is a local proof of the split general-linear specialization corroborated by Dudas--Michel Theorem 11.11, rather than an application of Taylor's spherical result to a nontrivial character without the twist and faithful induction argument.

items.title: The constituents of the spherical principal series of GL_n
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, used through Tits deformation. Let $G=\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$ and let $\mathbb C[G/B]$ be the permutation module on the complete flags. The set of isomorphism classes of simple constituents of $\mathbb C[G/B]$ is in bijection with the set $\{\lambda:\lambda\vdash n\}$ of partitions of $n$: the bijection is the composite of the endomorphism-algebra parametrisation of [[lem-constituent-multiplicities-under-a-semisimple-endomorphism-algebra]], the Tits isomorphism $\operatorname{End}_G(\mathbb C[G/B])\cong\mathbb C[S_n]$ of [[cor-type-a-finite-hecke-algebra-is-noncanonically-isomorphic-to-csn]] and the classification of the irreducible $\mathbb C[S_n]$-modules by partitions. Write $V_\lambda$ for the simple $\mathbb C[G]$-module attached to $\lambda$ by that bijection. Then $$\mathbb C[G/B]\;\cong\;\bigoplus_{\lambda\vdash n} V_\lambda^{\oplus f^\lambda},$$ where $f^\lambda=\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\lambda$ is the number of standard $\lambda$-tableaux, and the multiplicities satisfy $$\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_G\bigl(V_\lambda,\mathbb C[G/B]\bigr)=f^\lambda,\qquad \operatorname{End}_G\bigl(\mathbb C[G/B]\bigr)\cong\prod_{\lambda\vdash n}\operatorname M_{f^\lambda}(\mathbb C).$$ Equivalently, the constituents of the spherical principal series $I(1)$ are indexed by the partitions of $n$ and the constituent indexed by $\lambda$ occurs with multiplicity $f^\lambda$.
items.strategy: By Maschke $\mathbb C[G]$ is semisimple, so $\mathbb C[G/B]$ is a semisimple $\mathbb C[G]$-module and the endomorphism-algebra lemma [[lem-constituent-multiplicities-under-a-semisimple-endomorphism-algebra]] applies with $A=\mathbb C[G]$, $M=\mathbb C[G/B]$, $E=\operatorname{End}_G(\mathbb C[G/B])$: the constituents of $M$ are indexed by the simple $E$-modules and the multiplicity equals the dimension of the corresponding simple $E$-module. Now $E\cong H^{\mathrm{op}}\cong H$ where $H=e_B\mathbb C[G]e_B$ is the finite Hecke algebra ([[thm-finite-hecke-algebra-as-convolution-corner-and-endomorphisms]]), and $H\cong\mathbb C[S_n]$ by Tits deformation ([[cor-type-a-finite-hecke-algebra-is-noncanonically-isomorphic-to-csn]]). Irreducible $\mathbb C[S_n]$-modules are the Specht modules $S^\lambda$, $\lambda\vdash n$ ([[thm-complex-irreducibles-of-symmetric-groups-are-specht-modules]]), with dimensions $\dim S^\lambda=f^\lambda$ by the hook-length formula ([[thm-hook-length-formula]]). Transporting the simple modules and their dimensions along the isomorphism $E\cong\mathbb C[S_n]$ gives the stated bijection and multiplicities. The Axiom of Choice is carried from the Tits-deformation supplier; all remaining steps are finite-dimensional.

items.title: The constituents of a general finite principal series
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, used through Tits deformation. Let $G=\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$, $\chi\in\widehat T$ with equal-character blocks of sizes $n_1,\dots,n_k$ and Weyl stabiliser $W_\chi=S_{n_1}\times\cdots\times S_{n_k}$. Then the isomorphism classes of simple constituents of the principal series $I(\chi)$ are indexed by the tuples $(\lambda^{(1)},\dots,\lambda^{(k)})$ of partitions $\lambda^{(r)}\vdash n_r$, and the multiplicity of the constituent attached to such a tuple equals $$\prod_{r=1}^kf^{\lambda^{(r)}},$$ the product of the numbers of standard tableaux of the parts; equivalently $$\operatorname{End}_G\bigl(I(\chi)\bigr)\cong\prod_{(\lambda^{(1)},\dots,\lambda^{(k)})}\operatorname M_{\prod_rf^{\lambda^{(r)}}}(\mathbb C).$$ In particular, if $\chi$ is regular ($k=n$, all $n_r=1$) then $I(\chi)$ is irreducible, and if $\chi$ is trivial ($k=1$, $n_1=n$) the multiplicities are the hook-length numbers $f^\lambda$ of [[thm-spherical-principal-series-constituents-of-gl-n-fq]].
items.strategy: By Maschke $\mathbb C[G]$ is semisimple, so $I(\chi)$ is a semisimple $\mathbb C[G]$-module, and [[lem-constituent-multiplicities-under-a-semisimple-endomorphism-algebra]] applies with $E=\operatorname{End}_G(I(\chi))$: the constituents are indexed by the simple $E$-modules, with multiplicity equal to the dimension of the corresponding simple module. By [[thm-general-finite-principal-series-endomorphism-algebra]] one has $E\cong H_q(W_\chi)\cong\bigotimes_rH_q(S_{n_r})\cong\bigotimes_r\mathbb C[S_{n_r}]=\mathbb C[W_\chi]$. The simple $\mathbb C[S_{n_r}]$-modules are the Specht modules $S^{\lambda^{(r)}}$ ([[thm-complex-irreducibles-of-symmetric-groups-are-specht-modules]]) of dimensions $f^{\lambda^{(r)}}$ ([[thm-hook-length-formula]]); finite Wedderburn matrix decompositions of the factors tensor to matrix factors $M_a(\mathbb C)\otimes M_b(\mathbb C)\cong M_{ab}(\mathbb C)$ (send matrix-unit tensors to the corresponding pair-indexed matrix units). Thus the simple modules are the external tensor products, indexed by tuples, of dimension $\prod_rf^{\lambda^{(r)}}$, and the result follows. The regular and trivial cases are the boundary cases $n_r=1$ (only the partition $(1)$, $f^{(1)}=1$) and $k=1$. The Axiom of Choice is carried from the Tits-deformation supplier; all remaining steps are finite-dimensional.

items.title: The two-dimensional Hecke algebra for GL_2(F_q)
items.statement:
For $n=2$, $G=\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_q)$, $B$ the upper triangular Borel and
$e_B=|B|^{-1}\sum_{b\in B}b$, the finite Hecke algebra
$H=e_B\mathbb C[G]e_B$ has $\mathbb C$-basis $\{T_1=e_B,T_s\}$, where $s$ is the
nontrivial element of $S_2$ and $T_s=|B|^{-1}\sum_{x\in B\dot sB}x$, and the
multiplication is
$$T_s^2=(q-1)T_s+q\,T_1.$$
Hence $H\cong\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$ (the two projections onto the simple
$H$-modules), and the abstract presentation is
$H\cong\mathbb C[T]/(T^2-(q-1)T-q)$; for $q=2$ this is
$\mathbb C[T]/((T-2)(T+1))\cong\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$. The normalization is
the one fixed in
def-bruhat-double-coset-basis-of-the-finite-hecke-algebra; in particular
$\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{End}_G(\mathbb C[\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_q)])=2$
and the opposite-algebra ambiguity is invisible because
$H\cong H^{\mathrm{op}}$. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Specialise the general computations: the basis statement is [[def-bruhat-double-coset-basis-of-the-finite-hecke-algebra]], the quadratic relation is [[lem-rank-one-hecke-quadratic-relation]] and the presentation is [[thm-type-a-iwahori-hecke-presentation]] (the braid and commutation relations are vacuous for $n=2$). Semisimplicity and the splitting into two copies of $\mathbb C$ follow from $q\ne-1$ together with the explicit factorisation $T^2-(q-1)T-q=(T-q)(T+1)$ of the minimal polynomial of $T_s$; the two factors have distinct roots since $q\ge2$. No choice principle is used.

items.title: The trivial and Steinberg splitting on P^1(F_q)
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, used through Tits deformation. For $G=\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_q)$ the spherical principal series is the permutation module $\mathbb C[\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_q)]=\mathbb C[G/B]$ of dimension $q+1$, and it decomposes as $$\mathbb C[\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_q)]\;=\;\mathbf 1\;\oplus\;\operatorname{St},$$ where $\mathbf 1$ is the trivial representation and $\operatorname{St}$ is the Steinberg representation of dimension $q$; both occur with multiplicity $1$. Choose the noncanonical hook-length parametrisation so the Hecke character $T_s\mapsto q$ matches the trivial $S_2$ character and $T_s\mapsto-1$ the sign character. Under this parametrisation of [[thm-spherical-principal-series-constituents-of-gl-n-fq]] the trivial representation corresponds to $\lambda=(2)$ ($f^{(2)}=1$) and $\operatorname{St}$ to $\lambda=(1,1)$ ($f^{(1,1)}=1$). The standard Hecke generator $T_s$ acts on $\mathbf 1$ by the scalar $q$ and on $\operatorname{St}$ by the scalar $-1$, matching the two simple $H$-modules of [[ex-two-dimensional-hecke-algebra-for-gl2-fq]].
items.strategy: For $G=\operatorname{GL}_2$ the flag variety is $\mathbb P^1$, and $\mathbb C[\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_q)]=I(1)$ by [[lem-spherical-principal-series-is-the-flag-permutation-module]]. The equal-coordinate rank-one computation [[lem-equal-coordinate-rank-one-principal-series-of-gl2-fq]] with the trivial character $a=1$ gives the splitting $1\oplus\operatorname{St}$ with $\dim\operatorname{St}=q$, and identifies the $T_s$-eigenvalues as $q$ and $-1$. The multiplicities are also consistent with the general spherical formula [[thm-spherical-principal-series-constituents-of-gl-n-fq]] and the hook-length values $f^{(2)}=f^{(1,1)}=1$ ([[thm-hook-length-formula]]). The Axiom of Choice is carried from the Tits-deformation supplier; all remaining steps are finite-dimensional.

items.title: The q=2 torus boundary
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, used through Tits deformation. For $q=2$ the multiplicative group $\mathbb F_2^\times$ is trivial, so the diagonal torus $T\cong(\mathbb F_2^\times)^n$ is trivial and there is exactly one character $\chi=1$ of $T$ for every $n$: the regular case is empty for $n\ge2$ (for $n=1$ the unique coordinate is vacuously pairwise distinct), $W_\chi=S_n$ for all $n$, and every principal series is spherical, $I(\chi)=I(1)=\mathbb C[G/B]$. The general theorems remain valid: $\dim\operatorname{End}_G(I(1))=|S_n|=n!$, the constituents are indexed by partitions $\lambda\vdash n$ with multiplicities $f^\lambda$, and the finite Hecke algebra $H_q(n)$ at $q=2$ is semisimple (the quadratic relation is $T_i^2=T_i+2$, whose factors $T_i-2$ and $T_i+1$ have distinct roots), so Tits deformation still identifies $H_q(n)$ with $\mathbb C[S_n]$. The boundary phenomenon is the collapse of the parametrising torus and of the Weyl action, not a failure of the constituent description.
items.strategy: For $q=2$, $\mathbb F_2^\times=\{1\}$ and hence $T=\{I_n\}=\widehat T$; the unique character is fixed by all of $S_n$, so $W_\chi=S_n$ and the principal series is spherical, identified with the flag permutation module by [[lem-spherical-principal-series-is-the-flag-permutation-module]]. The constituent statement is [[thm-spherical-principal-series-constituents-of-gl-n-fq]]; semisimplicity of the Hecke algebra is the corner-of-Maschke argument of [[lem-semisimplicity-and-trace-form-for-the-finite-spherical-hecke-algebra]], and $2\ne-1$ ensures the quadratic polynomial has distinct roots. The Axiom of Choice is carried from the Tits-deformation supplier; all remaining steps are finite-dimensional.

items.title: Regular and singular torus characters in GL_3(F_q)
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, used through Tits deformation. Let $G=\operatorname{GL}_3(\mathbb F_q)$ and let $\chi=(\chi_1,\chi_2,\chi_3)\in\widehat T$; every principal series has dimension $[G:B]=(q+1)(q^2+q+1)$. (a) If the three coordinates are pairwise distinct, then $W_\chi=1$, $\operatorname{End}_G(I(\chi))=\mathbb C$ and $I(\chi)$ is irreducible. (b) If exactly two coordinates are equal, say $\chi=(a,a,b)$ with $a\ne b$, then $W_\chi\cong S_2$, $\dim\operatorname{End}_G(I(\chi))=2$ and $I(\chi)$ has exactly two non-isomorphic constituents, both of multiplicity $1$, corresponding to the two tuples $(\lambda^{(1)},\lambda^{(2)})$ with $\lambda^{(1)}\vdash2$, $\lambda^{(2)}\vdash1$, i.e. to $((2),(1))$ and $((1,1),(1))$, with multiplicities $f^{(2)}=f^{(1,1)}=1$. (c) If all three coordinates are equal, $\chi=(a,a,a)$, then $W_\chi=S_3$, $\dim\operatorname{End}_G(I(\chi))=6$, and $I(\chi)$ has $3$ pairwise non-isomorphic constituents indexed by the partitions $\lambda\vdash3$, with multiplicities $f^{(3)}=1$, $f^{(2,1)}=2$, $f^{(1,1,1)}=1$; equivalently $\operatorname{End}_G(I(\chi))\cong\mathbb C[S_3]$. In cases (b) and (c) the counting of constituents agrees with the general corollary, and in case (c) it also agrees with the spherical computation for $I(1)$ twisted by $a\circ\det$.
items.strategy: The statements combine: the dimension $[G:B]$ from [[def-principal-series-module-for-finite-gl-n]]; the irreducibility and endomorphism dimension from [[cor-regular-finite-principal-series-is-irreducible]] and [[thm-weyl-stabilizer-controls-principal-series-endomorphisms]]; the constituent indexing and multiplicities from [[cor-constituents-of-general-principal-series-for-finite-gl-n]]; the hook-length values $f^{(3)}=f^{(2,1)}=f^{(1,1,1)}=1,2,1$ from [[thm-hook-length-formula]]. For (c) one can also use the twist $I(a,a,a)\cong I(1)\otimes(a\circ\det)$ and the spherical theorem [[thm-spherical-principal-series-constituents-of-gl-n-fq]]. The Axiom of Choice is carried from the Tits-deformation supplier; all remaining steps are finite-dimensional.

items.title: The Tits isomorphism is non-canonical
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, used through Tits deformation. The isomorphism $H=e_B\mathbb C[G]e_B\cong\mathbb C[S_n]$ supplied by Tits deformation, and the consequent parametrisation of the constituents of a principal series by tuples of partitions, are not canonical: the deformation argument produces an isomorphism by deforming through the generic algebra, using an open subset of the parameter line, lifting idempotents, determinant inversion and a constructible incidence locus, and it does not canonically identify the standard basis $(T_w)$ with the group elements $(w)$ nor the simple $H$-modules with the Specht modules. Different choices in the deformation (or different specialisations of the generic algebra) can produce different isomorphisms, and downstream arguments must not treat the partition labelling of a single constituent as if it were canonical or compatible with every natural operation. What is canonical is the resulting numerical data: the number of simple constituents and the multiset of their multiplicities as dimensions of simple $\mathbb C[W_\chi]$-modules.
items.strategy:
The construction of [[thm-tits-deformation-for-the-type-a-hecke-algebra]] is an formal lifting and constructible incidence argument, none of whose steps selects an isomorphism of bases or a bijection of simple modules; Taylor's Remark 5.23 and the closing remark of Losev record explicitly that the bijection of irreducibles is not uniquely determined by the multiplicity statement. There is generally no algebra isomorphism sending every standard $T_w$ to $w$ when $q
e1$, because their quadratic relations differ; and the deformation isomorphism need not preserve the natural operations; the numerical invariants (dimensions of simple modules, hence the multiplicities in [[cor-constituents-of-general-principal-series-for-finite-gl-n]]) are independent of the choices. The Axiom of Choice is carried from the Tits-deformation supplier; all remaining steps are finite-dimensional.
